description: Create all API route handlers and the auth middleware. Depends on FEAT-001 (lib files must exist). These routes are what the updated frontend pages (FEAT-003) call.
steps: Step 1 — Create directory c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\app\api\submissions\ and file route.ts. GET handler: call getSubmissions() from lib/dynamodb.ts, return NextResponse.json(submissions). POST handler: parse request body, validate required fields (name, address, phone, amount, allocation, paymentMode — return 400 if any missing or amount not a positive number). Generate transactionId: 'MOI-' + String(Date.now()).slice(-6).padStart(6,'0') (deterministic enough for prototype, guaranteed unique in practice). Build a Submission object with timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), event: 'Suresh & Priya Wedding | Raja Mahal, Chennai'. Call putSubmission(submission) from lib/dynamodb.ts. Call sendReceiptEmail(submission) from lib/ses.ts (fire-and-forget, do not await or block response). Return NextResponse.json({ success: true, submission }, { status: 201 }). Both handlers must have explicit TypeScript return types (Promise<NextResponse>).

Step 2 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\app\api\submissions\[id]\route.ts. GET handler with params { params: { id: string } }: call getSubmissionById(params.id) from lib/dynamodb.ts. Return 404 if null, else return NextResponse.json(submission).

Step 3 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\app\api\export\route.ts. GET handler: call getSubmissions() from lib/dynamodb.ts. Build CSV string: header row '#,Transaction ID,Guest Name,Village/Address,Phone,Amount (INR),Gift For,Payment Mode,Date', then one row per submission quoting name and address fields with double-quotes and escaping any internal double-quotes. Return new NextResponse(csvContent, { status: 200, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/csv; charset=utf-8', 'Content-Disposition': 'attachment; filename="master-ledger.csv"' } }).

Step 4 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\app\api\auth\login\route.ts. POST handler: parse body for { password: string }. Call verifyAdminPassword(password) from lib/cognito.ts. If false return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: 'Invalid password' }, { status: 401 }). If true: call generateSessionToken() from lib/cognito.ts, create a NextResponse with body { success: true }, then set a cookie: response.cookies.set('lumapath_auth', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production', sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: 86400, path: '/' }). Return the response.

Step 5 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\app\api\auth\logout\route.ts. POST handler: create NextResponse with body { success: true }, delete the 'lumapath_auth' cookie by setting maxAge: 0. Return response.

Step 6 — Create c:\Users\laksh\OneDrive\Attachments\Desktop\LumaPath\middleware.ts at the project root (NOT inside app/). Protected routes: /bride, /groom, /ledger. Use NextRequest and NextResponse from 'next/server' only — no Node.js imports. Logic: get the cookie value with request.cookies.get('lumapath_auth')?.value. Import verifySessionToken from lib/cognito.ts — but because middleware runs in the Edge runtime, avoid importing the full lib/cognito.ts if it imports Node.js-only modules. Instead, inline the token verification logic directly in middleware.ts: decode the base64 token with atob(), parse JSON, check exp > Date.now(). If cookie missing or token invalid, return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url)). Export a config: { matcher: ['/bride', '/groom', '/ledger'] }.
